_help: Track C: Reporting verbs. Items are grouped by stage. See README.md, section 'How to add or edit an item'.
title: Reporting verbs

items.prompt: Put each verb in its group. How sure, or how strong, is the author?
items.rule: Tentative: suggest, propose. Neutral: state, report, note, describe. Strong: argue, claim, assert, maintain. Findings: find, show, demonstrate.
items.hint: Which verb is used for results from research?

items.rule: Tentative: suggest, propose. Neutral: state, report, note, describe. Strong: argue, claim, assert, maintain. Findings: find, show, demonstrate.
items.hint: Which verb puts forward an idea carefully?

items.prompt: Put each verb in its group. How sure, or how strong, is the author?
items.rule: Tentative: suggest, propose. Neutral: state, report, note, describe. Strong: argue, claim, assert, maintain. Findings: find, show, demonstrate.
items.hint: “Hypothesise” means to offer a possible explanation that still needs testing.

stages.title: Match the verb to the source

sourceCards.title: Bilingual children and attention
sourceCards.did: Ran an experiment with a large group of children and measured how fast they switched tasks.

items.prompt: Read what the author did. Which verb represents the source fairly?
items.frame: Tran (2020) ___ that bilingual children switched tasks faster than other children.
items.rule: Choose a verb that represents what the author really did: findings, a strong opinion, a neutral report or a careful proposal.
items.hint: The author has evidence from an experiment.

sourceCards.title: Rethinking the lecture
sourceCards.did: Gave a careful idea in the final section. Said it should be tested in future studies.

items.prompt: Read what the author did. Which verb represents the source fairly?
items.frame: Petrova (2021) ___ that shorter lectures might help students concentrate.
items.rule: Choose a verb that represents what the author really did: findings, a strong opinion, a neutral report or a careful proposal.
items.hint: The author is not sure yet. The idea is not tested.

sourceCards.title: The case for urban parks
sourceCards.did: Strongly disagreed with other writers and gave several reasons for this view. No new data.

items.prompt: Read what the author did. Which verb represents the source fairly?
items.frame: Haddad (2019) ___ that cities must build more green space.
items.rule: Choose a verb that represents what the author really did: findings, a strong opinion, a neutral report or a careful proposal.
items.hint: This is a strong opinion with reasons, not research results.

sourceCards.title: Student loans explained
sourceCards.did: Explained the steps of the repayment system, without giving an opinion.

items.prompt: Read what the author did. Which verb represents the source fairly?
items.frame: Achieng (2018) ___ how first-year students pay back their student loans after graduating.
items.rule: Choose a verb that represents what the author really did: findings, a strong opinion, a neutral report or a careful proposal.
items.hint: The author simply explains how something works.

sourceCards.title: Print or screen?
sourceCards.did: Carried out a survey of students and reported the answers.

items.prompt: Read what the author did. Which verb represents the source fairly?
items.frame: Duarte (2022) ___ that most students in the survey preferred printed books for long texts.
items.rule: Choose a verb that represents what the author really did: findings, a strong opinion, a neutral report or a careful proposal.
items.hint: The author has survey results.

sourceCards.title: Bike lanes for small towns
sourceCards.did: Put forward a new plan and said that more research is needed before towns use it.

items.prompt: Read what the author did. Which verb represents the source fairly?
items.frame: Volkov (2023) ___ a new way to plan bike lanes in small towns.
items.rule: Choose a verb that represents what the author really did: findings, a strong opinion, a neutral report or a careful proposal.
items.hint: A new idea, offered carefully.

sourceCards.title: Campus housing figures
sourceCards.did: Gave the numbers in a table, with no comment or opinion.

items.prompt: Read what the author did. Which verb represents the source fairly?
items.frame: Nakamura (2020) ___ the number of students living on campus each year.
items.rule: Choose a verb that represents what the author really did: findings, a strong opinion, a neutral report or a careful proposal.
items.hint: The author just presents facts, with no opinion.

sourceCards.title: Childhood without homework
sourceCards.did: Has defended this view in several books over many years, even though others disagree.

items.prompt: Read what the author did. Which verb represents the source fairly?
items.frame: Moretti (2017) ___ that homework should be banned in primary schools.
items.rule: Choose a verb that represents what the author really did: findings, a strong opinion, a neutral report or a careful proposal.
items.hint: The author keeps holding a strong view over time.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: According to Haddad (2019), cities need more green space.
According to Haddad (2019) {argues|argued} that cities need more green space.
According to Haddad (2019) that cities need more green space.
acceptedAnswers: According to Haddad (2019), cities need more green space.
items.rule: Use “According to Author (year), …” OR “Author (year) argues that …”, never both.
items.hint: “According to” already reports the idea. Does it need a reporting verb too?

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: Novak (2021) {suggests|suggested} that students should take regular breaks.
Novak (2021) {suggests|suggested} students to take regular breaks.
acceptedAnswers: Novak (2021) {suggests|suggested} that students should take regular breaks.
items.rule: “Suggest” is followed by a that-clause, not “to + verb”.
items.hint: After “suggest”, what kind of word comes next?

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: Okafor (2020) {describes|described} the process of applying for a student visa.
Okafor (2020) {describes|described} that applying for a student visa is a long process.
Okafor (2020) {describes|described} about the process of applying for a student visa.
acceptedAnswers: Okafor (2020) {describes|described} the process of applying for a student visa.
items.rule: “Describe” takes a noun phrase (describe something), not a that-clause.
items.hint: “Describe” needs an object: describe something.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: Kim (2018) {discusses|discussed} the effects of noise on sleep.
Kim (2018) {discusses|discussed} about the effects of noise on sleep.
acceptedAnswers: Kim (2018) {discusses|discussed} the effects of noise on sleep.
items.rule: “Discuss” takes a noun phrase (discuss something), with no “about” and no that-clause.
items.hint: Do we say “discuss about”?

items.prompt: Which verb can NOT be followed by “that”?
items.rule: Verbs like describe, discuss and outline take a noun phrase. Verbs like argue, find, suggest and note can take a that-clause.
items.hint: Try each verb with “… that students need more sleep.”

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: According to Pillai (2020), noise makes concentration harder.
According to (Pillai, 2020), noise makes concentration harder.
According to Pillai, 2020, noise makes concentration harder.
acceptedAnswers: According to Pillai (2020), noise makes concentration harder.
items.rule: After “According to”, write a narrative citation: According to Pillai (2020), …
items.hint: After “According to”, the author's name is part of the sentence.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: As Tran (2019) {notes|noted}, bilingual children may switch tasks more easily.
As Tran (2019) {notes|noted} that bilingual children may switch tasks more easily.
As noted Tran (2019), bilingual children may switch tasks more easily.
acceptedAnswers: As Tran (2019) {notes|noted}, bilingual children may switch tasks more easily.
items.rule: “As Author (year) notes, …” is followed by a comma and a full clause, with no “that”.
items.hint: “As … notes,” already introduces the idea.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: Varga (2014) {outlines|outlined} three ways to review lecture notes.
Varga (2014) {outlines|outlined} that there are three ways to review lecture notes.
Varga (2014) {outlines|outlined} about three ways to review lecture notes.
acceptedAnswers: Varga (2014) {outlines|outlined} three ways to review lecture notes.
items.rule: “Outline” takes a noun phrase: outline something.
items.hint: “Outline” needs an object: outline something.

items.prompt: Which verb form fits the gap? Check the subject.
items.frame: Moreau (2019) ___ that public libraries help students from all backgrounds.
items.rule: One author is singular: argues / argued / has argued.
items.hint: One author. Singular or plural?

items.prompt: Which verb form fits the gap? Check the subject.
items.frame: Kaur and Novak (2020) ___ that music with lyrics makes reading harder.
items.rule: Two authors, or et al., are plural: argue / argued / have argued.
items.hint: Two authors. Singular or plural?

items.prompt: Which verb form fits the gap? Check the subject.
items.frame: Abebe et al. (2022) ___ that refill stations reduce plastic waste.
items.rule: Two authors, or et al., are plural: argue / argued / have argued.
items.hint: “et al.” means “and others”. Singular or plural?

items.prompt: Which verb form fits the gap? Check the subject.
items.frame: Ferreira (2015) ___ that homework can build a useful link between school and home.
items.rule: One author is singular: argues / argued / has argued.
items.hint: One author. Look at “has” and “have” too.

items.prompt: Which verb form fits the gap? Check the subject.
items.frame: Tanaka and Brennan (2019) ___ that students read more before exams.
items.rule: Two authors, or et al., are plural: argue / argued / have argued.
items.hint: Two authors. Look at “has” and “have” too.

items.prompt: Which verb form fits the gap? Check the subject.
items.frame: Nguyen et al. (2023) ___ that working from home suits some jobs better than others.
items.rule: Two authors, or et al., are plural: argue / argued / have argued.
items.hint: “et al.” is plural.

items.prompt: Rewrite the sentence with a better verb than “says”. Read what the author did first.
items.frame: Haddad (2019) says that cities need much more green space for the health of residents.
modelAnswers: Haddad (2019) {argues|argued} that cities need much more green space for the health of residents.
Haddad (2019) {maintains|maintained} that cities need much more green space for the health of residents.
items.rule: Replace “says” with a verb that shows what the author did: found, argued, suggested, described …
items.hint: A strong opinion with reasons.

Abebe et al. (2022) {demonstrate|demonstrated} that refill stations reduce plastic waste.
